# lean-pkg receipt check

validate a published package's receipts from git alone: no registry, no network, never runs Lean (an outside referee's check; exit 0 only when every check passes).

Also spelled: `lean-pkg verify-receipts` ([all aliases](aliases.md)).

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg receipt check --repo DIR --commit SHA [--at REF] [--docs-descendants]
                       [--evidence-only] [--name NAME] [--corroborate]
                       [--github OWNER/REPO] [--json]
```

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--repo DIR` | a local clone of the package (the package directory; cloned privately, never modified). Required. |
| `--commit SHA` | the commit the receipts bind (the page's `git checkout <commit>` line). Required. |
| `--at REF` | the published ref whose .lean-receipts/, coverage.yaml and README.md are read (default HEAD of --repo); it must be the commit or an evidence-only descendant of it (or a docs-only one, when the docs-only rule applies) |
| `--docs-descendants` | for a package without lean-pkg-binding.yaml at the commit: also accept a docs-only descendant (no build input changed) as the referee's choice, printed in the result; a committed file that says false or does not validate overrides it |
| `--evidence-only` | accept only evidence-only descendants: ignore the author's committed opt-in (lean-pkg-binding.yaml at the commit, applied by default) |
| `--name NAME` | the package name the claims must carry (default: `package` in coverage.yaml, else claims.yaml, else the directory name) |
| `--corroborate` | also corroborate every receipt with a ci block (a GitHub Actions run) against the public GitHub REST API, level 2, and fail when one does not reach it (404, rate limit, network error and a redirect off api.github.com fail closed). GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, when set, only raises the rate limit and is never printed. The one networked check |
| `--github OWNER/REPO` | with --corroborate: the package's own GitHub repository, whose numeric id the run's must equal (default: the receipt's ci.repository, and the output says so) |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `receipt check` | an outside referee's check of a published package: reads no registry, opens no network connection and never runs Lean. Clones `--repo` privately (local transport only; its working tree is never read or changed), checks out the published ref (`--at`, default HEAD) and runs `gate`'s and `comparator`'s own validators on the receipts under `.lean-receipts/` that bind `--commit` (a JSON file named for the commit that is not a receipt fails, unless its `schema` is one of the comparator runner's own records, such as `comparator-stages/1`, which is skipped and listed): the binding (evidence-only descendants, with `gate`'s exemption for a `formalization.yaml` at the package root that differs only in derived keys, printed when applied; docs-only ones too when `lean-pkg-binding.yaml` committed at the commit opts in, by default, reported first as an `opt-in` check (`PASS`, or `SKIP` with the reason for a file that says `false`, does not validate, was added after the commit, or is ignored by `--evidence-only`); for a package without that file, with `--docs-descendants`, the referee's choice, printed with the result, which a committed `false` or invalid file overrides; never with `--evidence-only`; the `rule:` line says which rule bound and who chose it, `--json` `docs_descendants`, `evidence_only` and `opt_in {source, commit, path, build_inputs, file, problems}`), the toolchain and Mathlib pins at the commit, every SHA-256 (configurations, logs, the redacted verify log, `manifest_sha256` and the other additive evidence keys, the olean manifest record), the claims at the commit, the comparator configurations naming every reusable theorem claim, `coverage.yaml` (R11) and the README page block against the receipts. One line per check, `PASS`, `FAIL` or `SKIP` (not applicable, with the reason); `--json` lists them all. A toolchain on lean-pkg's toolchain advisories list adds one `WARN: toolchain advisory ...` line per entry after the verdict, never a failure (JSON `toolchain_advisories[]`; [toolchain advisories](../receipts.md#checking-a-published-packages-receipts-receipt-check)). `--corroborate` is the one networked check: each receipt with a `ci` block (a GitHub Actions run) is corroborated against the public GitHub REST API (level 2: the attempt it names completed with success on the commit, in the package's repository by numeric id, a job on a GitHub-hosted runner, exactly one `lean-pkg-receipt` annotation binding the committed receipt and log bytes, the workflow calling lean-pkg's pinned `verify.yml` at a 40-hex commit whose content is in the shipped pin list), one `ci level 2 CHECK` row per check, failing when it does not reach level 2; a 404, 403 or 429 (naming `GH_TOKEN`), a network error and a redirect off api.github.com fail closed. `--github OWNER/REPO` names the package's repository (default: the receipt's `ci.repository`, printed); `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` only raises the rate limit and is never printed or written; `--json` gains `ci {level, rows[]}`, `github` and `network: true` ([level 2](../receipts.md#corroborating-the-run-level-2---corroborate)). Exit 0 only when no check fails, 1 otherwise, 2 on a usage error (`--docs-descendants` with `--evidence-only` is one). Re-running Lean is the comparator step of docs/trust-model.md, "Re-verify a page yourself". The 1.0 command tree's read-only verb on the `receipt` noun; the spelling `verify-receipts` is reserved for its alias table | `--repo DIR` `--commit SHA` `--at REF` `--docs-descendants` `[--corroborate [--github OWNER/REPO]]` `--evidence-only` `--json` |

## Examples

In a fresh clone of a published package, check its receipts for the page's bound commit from git alone; no registry, no network, no Lean run.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt check --repo . --commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
```

Sample output:

```text
receipt check: PASS my-proof at 0123456789ab (tier comparator; 13 passed, 1 skipped)
  commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 (published ref 89abcdef0123)
  rule: evidence-only descendants (docs-only not accepted; --docs-descendants to accept them)
  ...
  PASS binding: evidence-only descendant of 0123456789ab (+3 evidence file(s))
  ...
receipt check: PASS my-proof at 0123456789ab (tier comparator; 13 passed, 1 skipped)
```

At a release tag after the page commit, for a package that committed lean-pkg-binding.yaml at the bound commit; its opt-in to the docs-only rule is applied without a flag, and the binding line lists what changed.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt check --repo . --commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --at v1.0.0
```

Sample output:

```text
receipt check: PASS my-proof at 0123456789ab (tier comparator; 14 passed, 1 skipped)
  commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 (published ref 89abcdef0123)
  rule: evidence-only or docs-only descendants (docs-only: the author's opt-in, lean-pkg-binding.yaml committed at 0123456789ab; --evidence-only to refuse them)
  ...
  PASS opt-in: lean-pkg-binding.yaml at 0123456789ab opts in to docs-only descendants (build_inputs: 0 glob(s))
  PASS binding: docs-only descendant of 0123456789ab (1 non-build file(s): README.md; opted in at 0123456789ab by lean-pkg-binding.yaml)
  ...
receipt check: PASS my-proof at 0123456789ab (tier comparator; 14 passed, 1 skipped)
```

The strict rule over the author's committed opt-in, where only an evidence-only descendant binds; every check with its verdict as JSON.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt check --repo . --commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --at v1.0.0 --evidence-only --json
```

For a package without lean-pkg-binding.yaml, also accept a README or notes committed after the evidence (the docs-only rule, the referee's choice); every check with its verdict as JSON.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt check --repo . --commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --at v1.0.0 --docs-descendants --json
```

Also corroborate a GitHub Actions receipt against the public run API (level 2), the package's repository named by --github; GH_TOKEN only raises the rate limit.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt check --repo . --commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --corroborate --github OWNER/REPO
```
